title: A Comprehensive Protocol for Bayesian Phylogenetic Analysis Using MrBayes
author: Jinxing Wang
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Basic operation of the GUIDANCE2 website
Import a NEXUS file using the Execute mode

steps.title: Align sequences with GUIDANCE2
steps.instruction: Perform a MAFFT alignment via the GUIDANCE2 web server, ensuring proper FASTA formatting and optional parameter tuning.

substeps.instruction: Open the GUIDANCE2 server in a web browser.
Upload your multi‑sequence FASTA file; verify that each header starts with ">" and that sequence names contain only letters, numbers, or underscores.
Select MAFFT as the alignment method.
Configure advanced MAFFT options if desired (default settings are recommended). Optional tuning:
• Pairwise method choice:
– 6mer (fast, short sequences)
– localpair (local similarity, handles indels)
– genafpair (global alignment for longer sequences)
– globalpair (global alignment for similar‑length sequences).
Click **Submit** and wait for the job to finish.
Download the resulting alignment file (FASTA format).
Visually inspect the alignment to confirm correct placement of residues.
On the GUIDANCE2 results page, identify and remove unreliable columns as indicated; download the cleaned alignment.

steps.title: Convert alignment to NEXUS
steps.instruction: Transform the FASTA alignment into NEXUS format and ensure it is non‑interleaved for downstream tools.

substeps.instruction: Open MEGA, import the FASTA alignment, and export it as a NEXUS file.
Launch PAUP*.
In PAUP*, use **File → Open** and select the NEXUS file exported from MEGA.
Enter the following PAUP command to produce a non‑interleaved NEXUS file and execute it:
export file=filename.nex format=nexus interleaved=no
Replace *filename.nex* with your desired output name (often the same as the input).
Confirm that all sequence names contain only letters, numbers, or underscores.

steps.title: Select protein model with ProtTest
steps.instruction: Identify the best‑fit amino‑acid substitution model using ProtTest and extract the result automatically.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the protein alignment in FASTA or PHYLIP format.
Install Java (if not present) and download the latest ProtTest release from its GitHub repository.
Open a terminal, navigate to the ProtTest directory, and run:
java -jar prottest-3.4.2.jar -i <input_alignment> -o <output_file> -all-distributions -F -AIC -BIC -tc 0.5 -threads 12
Replace <input_alignment> and <output_file> with your filenames.
Install required Python packages:
pip install pandas tqdm
Create a Python script (e.g., *parse_prottest_output.py*) with the provided code, setting:
file_path = r"<ProtTest_output_file>"
output_path = r"<desired_CSV_path>"
Run the script:
python parse_prottest_output.py
Open the generated CSV and locate the model with the lowest AIC or BIC score; this model will be used for MrBayes.
Optional: keep the original ProtTest output for reference.

steps.title: Select nucleotide model with MrModeltest
steps.instruction: Determine the optimal nucleotide substitution model using MrModeltest and parse the scores automatically.

substeps.instruction: Ensure your nucleotide alignment is saved as a non‑interleaved NEXUS file (.nex).
Open PAUP*, load the NEXUS file, and then load the *MrModelblock* file found in the *MrModeltest2‑v.2.4/doc/* directory.
PAUP* will generate a *mrmodel.scores* file in the current working directory.
From a command‑line terminal, execute:
mrmodeltest2 out.txt
This reads *mrmodel.scores* and writes the model‑selection results to *out.txt* (rename as desired).
Create a Python script (e.g., *parse_mrmodeltest_output.py*) using the supplied code. Set:
file_path = "out.txt"
output_csv = "model_results.csv"
Install the required Python package:
pip install chardet
Run the script:
python parse_mrmodeltest_output.py
Open the resulting CSV and select the model with the highest lnL (log‑likelihood) value; this model will be used for MrBayes.

steps.title: Run MrBayes analysis
steps.instruction: Execute Bayesian phylogenetic inference in MrBayes using the selected substitution model.

substeps.instruction: Copy the final NEXUS file into the folder containing *mb.exe* (or ensure *mb* is in your PATH).
Open a command prompt (or PowerShell with ./ prefix) in that folder and start MrBayes:
mb
At the MrBayes prompt, load the NEXUS file:
execute your_file_name.nexus
Optionally disable the Beagle library to avoid compatibility issues:
set usebeagle=no
Open the supplemental Word file (Table S1 or S2) and locate the desired model/parameter combination (e.g., LG + I+G+F).
Enter the corresponding MrBayes commands, for example:
prset aamodelpr = fixed(LG);
prset statefreqpr = fixed(empirical);
lset rates = invgamma;
Start the MCMC run with the recommended settings:
mcmc ngen=1000000 samplefreq=100 printfreq=1000 diagnfreq=1000 nchains=4;
• ngen=1,000,000 (adjustable if convergence is poor)
• samplefreq=100 (keep default)
• printfreq=1000 and diagnfreq=1000 (output only)
• nchains=4 (standard parallel chains).
After the run finishes, summarize the tree and parameters:
sumt burnin=250;
sump burnin=250;
Export the posterior tree for visualization:
sumptrees filename=your_tree.t burnin=250;
Open the resulting *.t* file with iTol (https://itol.embl.de) by clicking **Upload a tree**.

steps.title: Validate phylogenetic trees
steps.instruction: Confirm the workflow by reproducing the benchmark analyses described in the protocol.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the validation datasets (LBP nucleotide sequences and BPI protein sequences) from the supplementary Materials (Datasets S1 and S2).
For the LBP nucleotide set, run MrBayes with 1,000,000 MCMC generations (as in step 5).
For the BPI protein set, run MrBayes with 2,000,000 MCMC generations.
After each run, inspect posterior probabilities on the resulting trees; high values indicate strong support and confirm protocol reproducibility.
